subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw allow SKILL.md metadata to declare scheduled or event-triggered autonomous execution, and what permission/provenance contract must gate that behavior?
rationale: This would turn installed skill metadata into an automation authority rather than passive instructions, so the safe product boundary cannot be inferred from current code alone.

options.title: Design Permissioned Core Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and specify the approved metadata placement, operator approval, revocation, cron/event mapping, and audit semantics before implementation.

options.title: Documentation-Only Metadata First
options.body: Accept only a non-executing trigger_description or audit hint now, leaving automatic registration for a later security-reviewed design.

options.title: Use Explicit Cron/Plugin APIs Only
options.body: Reject autonomous SKILL.md scheduling and document that skills may describe cron setup but must not register jobs without an explicit operator/plugin action.

recommendation.title: Design Permissioned Core Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and specify the approved metadata placement, operator approval, revocation, cron/event mapping, and audit semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current skill metadata/prompt and cron-adjacent source history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the concrete API boundary.
